mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS decline, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of UNRATE spike events, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction that pressures corporate revenue growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of joint HOUST/RSAFS decline periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 110 with monthly growth above 1.0% signals industrial overcapacity that reduces profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of INDPRO overcapacity events, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 5-year rolling periods.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 4.5% signals monetary tightening that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of FEDFUNDS > 4.5% periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of PAYEMS growth periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation environments (CPIAUCSL yoy > 2.0%), a decline in real consumer spending (RSAFS) signals reduced purchasing power that lowers corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation with real spending decline
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of high-inflation/RSAFS decline events, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) signals robust household demand that supports corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of RSAFS growth periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
